segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Forty. Equal triangles on equal bases and on the same side lie in the same parallels. Let triangles A B C and C D E be equal in area, standing on equal bases B C and C E on the same straight line B E and on the same side of it. We prove that the segment A D joining their vertices is parallel to base B E.

segments.text: Join point A to point D with segment A D. Suppose segment A D is not parallel to segment B E. Then by Proposition Thirty-One, through point A draw segment A F parallel to segment B E, meeting segment C D at point F, and join point F to point E.

segments.text: Since triangles A B C and F C E stand on equal bases B C and C E and lie in the same parallels B E and A F, by Proposition Thirty-Eight, triangle A B C equals triangle F C E. Yet by hypothesis, triangle A B C equals triangle D C E. By Common Notion One, things equal to the same thing are equal to one another, so triangle D C E equals triangle F C E, the greater equal to the less, which is impossible. Thus segment A F cannot be parallel to segment B E, nor can any other line through point A except segment A D. Therefore segment A D is parallel to segment B E, as was required to prove.
